title: Git & CI/CD
concept: Set up Git-based CI/CD for XIOM projects — automated builds, tests, linting, and verification on every push and pull request.
why: Manual testing doesn't scale. CI/CD automates quality checks: every push runs tests, lint, and verification. You catch bugs before they reach teammates.
theory:
## Automated Quality Gates

### Git Hooks

```sh
# .git/hooks/pre-commit (local)
#!/bin/sh
xiom fmt --check src/ || exit 1
xiom lint --deny-warnings src/ || exit 1
xiom test || exit 1
```

### Git Attributes

```
# .gitattributes
*.xi text eol=lf
*.lock binary
```

### CI Pipeline Stages

```yaml
# Typical CI pipeline for XIOM projects
stages:
  - format       # Check code formatting
  - lint         # Static analysis
  - build        # Compile the project
  - test         # Run unit tests
  - verify       # Static contract verification (optional)
  - benchmark    # Performance regression check
  - package      # Create distributable artifact
```

### CI Configuration

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml (see L6-24 for full example)
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: xiom-lang/setup-xiom@v1
        with:
          xiom-version: stable
      - run: xiom fmt --check src/
      - run: xiom lint --deny-warnings src/
      - run: xiom test
      - run: xiom build --release
```

### What to CI

- **Every push**: format, lint, test (fast checks)
- **Pull requests**: format, lint, test, build, verify (full checks)
- **Main branch**: format, lint, test, build, verify, benchmark (fullest checks)
- **Tags/releases**: all of above + package + publish

### Branch Strategy

```
main         ← production-ready code
├── feat/*   ← new features
├── fix/*    ← bug fixes
└── release/* ← release preparation
```

# CI runs the same commands — local and CI are consistent
tips: CI should mirror your local dev workflow — same commands, same flags
Fast checks first (format, lint) — fail early before expensive compilation
Cache build artifacts in CI — dramatically speeds up subsequent runs
Add status badges to your README — shows build status at a glance
common_mistakes: Running different commands in CI vs locally — CI green but local broken
Not caching dependencies — every CI run downloads everything from scratch
Long-running CI that discourages frequent commits — keep the basic pipeline under 5 minutes
